name: Structural priors applied per-frame (all backfired)
what_was_tried: Apply game-supplied exact constraints (verified true of this half's GT: exactly 22 detections/frame, 11 per team, 23 identities, jersey unique within team, no referees) post-hoc to the finished 45-minute predictions, per frame. Pipeline's unconstrained team split was 45.9/54.1 where truth is 50/50.

Both together: 14.674 (DetA 10.857, AssA 19.835) = -3.42. The per-frame team prior IMPROVED per-detection team accuracy 76.17% -> 82.86% (on 36,683 matched pairs) and still lost 1.74 GS-HOTA, via 124,186 team-label flips inside tracklets.

name: Track-level team prior (best score measured)
what_was_tried: Same 11-per-team prior, but committed at track level: one team per tracklet. Post-hoc on saved predictions, not an end-to-end pipeline change.
numbers: 11-per-team -> one team per tracklet: GS-HOTA 19.724 (DetA 16.567, AssA 23.493), +1.63 vs 18.094 — best measured on this half (+9% relative). One team per tracklet decided once: 19.295 (DetA 15.962, AssA 23.333), +1.20. Same prior per-frame vs per-track is a 3.37-point swing from placement alone; track-level variants produce zero label flips vs 124,186 per-frame. Caveat: post-hoc, not validated by an end-to-end rerun.

name: Jersey uniqueness constraints (track level)
what_was_tried: Force jersey numbers unique within a team at track level, with and without a support threshold; also try nulling weak jerseys instead.
numbers: Unique within team (any support): 17.569 (DetA 11.375, AssA 27.140) — the largest AssA gain seen anywhere (+4.8) yet still loses overall. Support >= 100: 17.230 (DetA 10.789, AssA 27.518). Nulling weak jerseys: 19.724 — changes nothing (pipeline already nulls those tracklets). Reason: median per-tracklet jersey support is 0.0; 75% of tracklets carry no jersey evidence at all.

name: Post-hoc identity re-grouping of tracklets
what_was_tried: Re-group the 347 tracklets into 58 identities by appearance-based merging under a hard temporal-exclusion constraint (two formulations: greedy closest-pair merging; largest-first slot colouring), verified to be using the new ids.

Tracklets are mixtures of ~13 players, not fragments of one — they would have to be split, so association must be fixed in the online tracker.

But it crosses over: 30s tracklet-level 40.352 vs detection-level 37.155; 1 min 57.824 vs 47.589; 2 min — vs 39.882; 5 min 19.484 vs 30.974. No single best team module across lengths; any length sweep must fix one config.

numbers: Measured -2.9 and -8.1 GS-HOTA. Default reverted to homography_objective: pixel. Kept as a negative result so the experiment is not repeated.

name: vitpose_strided (strided pose detector)
what_was_tried: Stride ViTPose to cut its dominant share of pipeline runtime.
numbers: Sub-2x speedup cost too much accuracy (exact accuracy delta not recorded in the source). Not in use.

name: merge_dataframes de-quadratification (TrackLab engine.py)
what_was_tried: Per-batch results were merged by rebuilding the whole accumulated detections frame each batch — O(len(frame)) twice over per batch, quadratic total, the main reason 45-minute halves were projected at ~63 h. Fixed in place.
numbers: Before: 1.02 s/batch at batch 0 rising to 3.74 s/batch by batch 2353. After: flat 0.90-0.97 s/batch. Validated on a full 750-frame pipeline run before and after: GS-HOTA 29.135% both times, metric summary files byte-identical, only prediction differences were float noise at 3.9e-11 m.

name: forget_columns applied at module end, deleted in place (offline.py)
what_was_tried: TrackerState only applied forget_columns at video teardown, so PRTReID's body_masks (1x64x32 float32, 8 KB/detection, unread downstream) was carried through all eleven remaining modules. First fix attempt used drop(columns=...) which freed nothing because EngineDatapipe holds a reference to the frame; fixed by deleting columns in place.
numbers: body_masks carried: 2.5 GB at 10 minutes, 11 GB at 45 minutes. On a 60,000-row stand-in: drop(columns=...) leaves 0.65 GB live (WORSE than the 0.58 GB before — two frames instead of one); del detections[col] in place leaves 0.08 GB. Caveat stated in source: this does NOT explain the 10-minute OOM, which occurred at 61% through PRTReID before this fix takes effect.

name: OptimizationConsistency O(N^2) fix (build_track_evidence + process)
what_was_tried: build_track_evidence iterated the track_id column's VALUES (once per detection, not per unique id), rebuilding a full-length mask each time; repeats overwrote each other identically. Replaced with one grouped pass (ddof=0 stated explicitly to match np.std vs pandas defaults). process had the same shape; replaced with groupby('image_id', sort=True) writing back only role_detection.
numbers: The module produced no output for 2 h 22 m on five minutes of footage; projected 25-45 hours on a 45-minute half — larger than all GPU stages combined. On the real 30-second state (15,642 detections, 26 tracklets): 107.798 s -> 0.006 s, 18,920x faster, worst field difference 0.000e+00 (bit-identical).

name: GTA tracklet distance made linear (refine_tracklets.py)
what_was_tried: get_distance materialised three full n1 x n2 GPU tensors to compute one scalar (mean pairwise cosine distance). Replaced with the exact separable identity: mean = 1 - dot(mean(a), mean(b)) for unit-normalised features, O(n1+n2) instead of O(n1*n2).
numbers: GPU memory by length (x3 tensors): 5 min 0.68 GB; 10 min 2.70 GB; 15 min 6.08 GB; 45 min 54.88 GB (single largest pair matrix 18.29 GB) against a 16 GB GPU with ~7.3 GB already held by models. After fix at 45 min: 54.88 GB -> 0.28 GB, a 198x reduction. Exactness verified to float32 rounding: worst difference 5.96e-08 vs float32 eps 1.19e-07, over tracklet sizes to 6000x6000, overlapping-times short circuit still returns 1.0. Caveat: no full pipeline run has yet confirmed identical GS-HOTA before/after.

name: 10-minute OOM root cause: glibc arena retention (malloc_trim fix)
what_was_tried: The 10-minute run was OOM-killed 61% through PRTReID with 35.5 GB on the parent's heap while the detections frame held 0.23 GB (~99% of resident memory not live). Five hypotheses refuted by measurement (frame columns, forget_columns, worker copy-on-write, per-module worker accumulation, glibc dynamic mmap threshold); diagnosis: glibc per-thread arena retention. Fix: malloc_trim(0) every 100 batches (TRACKLAB_MALLOC_TRIM=100).
numbers: Growth (GB per 100 batches): 2 min full 3-module 0.067; 5 min reid alone 0.075; 10 min reid alone 0.067; 10 min [bbox_detector, reid] 0.059; 10 min FULL pipeline 1.97 — detection count flat across 4.5x range so N is not the driver. With malloc_trim: PRTReID peaked at 16.34 GB vs 41.66 GB and climbing to a projected 87 GB; 58.2 GB reclaimed across 69 trim events; parent RSS steady ~5 GB; full 14-module run completed. Anti-pattern recorded: tracemalloc itself accounted for ~10 GB in one measurement and produced a false 'found it'.

name: Memory-claim retraction: PSS not RSS; orphaned workers
what_was_tried: Retract the report's claim that 'memory is not a constraint' (based on parent-only RSS on runs of 5 min and under); re-measure all figures as PSS across the process tree; document the orphaned dataloader-worker leak.
numbers: A tree reading 43 GB of RSS was 12.9 GB of PSS (12 forked workers share pages). Refuted: workers do not accumulate across module boundaries (count holds at 12). Real leak: children of an OOM-killed parent are reparented to init and never reaped — twelve found alive 23 hours later holding 8.79 GB PSS.

name: connect_track.py fixes (role AttributeError; pixel-vs-metre thresholds)

name: Per-attribute cost measurement (30 s / 1 min)
what_was_tried: Toggled one scorer flag at a time to price each attribute against the attributes-off ceiling; raw accuracy measured on geometry-matched pairs within 2 m.

name: Abstention (null attributes) as a lever
what_was_tried: Forced jersey -> null and team -> null to test whether abstaining on uncertain attributes helps, since a null maps to a class the ground truth does not contain.
numbers: jersey -> null scores 6.19 against a 37.155 baseline; team -> null scores 0.00. Abstention is punished, not rewarded — confidence thresholding is not a lever, only genuine accuracy is.

name: Jersey-number failure diagnosed as a funnel, not a model defect
what_was_tried: Traced detections through the jersey-reading pipeline stages.
numbers: total detections 31,107 (100%); jersey region proposed 926 (3.0%); read at confidence >= 0.8: 496 (1.6%); tracklets with >= 1 reading: 8 of 65 (12%); distinct numbers emitted 6-7 of 21 in GT. Median player box 25x55 px; median torso region 132 px^2 (~12x11 px). Gate min_roi_area=500 passes just 6.9% of detections; shoulder confidence is not the constraint (97.8% pass).

name: Team-fix variant matrix (attr_matrix) — variants that did not help
what_was_tried: A matrix of attribute-fix variants (read from attr_matrix.csv at report time) evaluated at short lengths.
numbers: Report's verdict: 'All flat.' Explanation embedded: team costs under 4 points at these lengths, so nothing improving team can move a score dominated by a 41-point jersey deficit; they should pay at 5 minutes, where team accuracy collapses to 51.6%. (Per-variant numbers live in attr_matrix.csv, not embedded in the script.)

name: Pose-derived foot anchor (ViTPose ankles instead of box bottom-middle)
what_was_tried: Replace the bounding-box bottom-middle ground anchor with the ViTPose ankle joint for pitch localisation.
numbers: 19% worse localisation: 1.139 -> 1.357 m. The ankle joint sits above the ground-contact point; the box bottom, ~5.5 px below the ankles, approximates it better.

name: Metre-space homography fitting
what_was_tried: Fit the homography in metres instead of pixels, since m/px varies 9x across the pitch depth.
numbers: Far-half keypoint residual improved 3.98 -> 2.45 m, but GS-HOTA got worse: 37.155 -> 34.268 at 30 s, 33.471 -> 25.383 at 1 min. The near half degraded and most players are on the near half. Lesson: p90 keypoint residual is a poor proxy for GS-HOTA (weights all pitch locations equally, players do not).

name: Jersey region gate loosening (min_roi_area / min_obb_ar)
what_was_tried: Loosened two configuration values in modules/jersey_number_det/pose_based_jn_det, turning sequence length from a liability into an asset (more read attempts per player accumulate into a correct per-tracklet majority vote). Full grid values read from jersey_sweep.csv at report time.
numbers: Headline embedded in KPI: 1 min with jersey gates fixed = 57.82 vs 33.47 baseline (+24.35). Baseline gates are area 500, ar 0.6. Caveat embedded: values were first explored on 128057 which is in the reported test split (fitting to the evaluation); a tuning grid on 117093 (valid split) is running so values are selected on non-reported data, then verified on 128057 — until then treat 250/100 and 0.3/0.6 as exploratory. Optima disagree between lengths: 250/0.3 best at 30 s, 100/0.6 at 1 min.

name: 117093 staging/alignment verification (valid-split tuning prerequisite)
what_was_tried: Independently verified 117093's alignment after staging, before using it for threshold selection.
numbers: Residual lag +2 frames (0.08 s), correlation 0.99949 — the 25-frame offset is correct for this match too. Its much lower absolute scores are genuine match difficulty, not a staging fault. (Grid values live in tune_117093.csv, not embedded.)

name: Degradation with sequence length: tracklet-level vs detection-level team, crossover
what_was_tried: One match (128057, 1st half), nested prefixes of identical footage, comparing stock tracklet-level team clustering against detection-level team assignment across lengths.
numbers: Both configurations peak at 1 minute and fall away on either side, and they cross over: stock tracklet-level is better at 30 s and 1 min (40.4 / 57.8 vs 37.2 / 47.6) and clearly worse by 5 min (19.5 vs 31.0). Mechanism: fragmentation — predicted tracklets go 26 -> 35 -> 42 -> 60 against 22 real players. Team accuracy at 5 min under stock clustering is 51.6% (indistinguishable from chance on two classes); detection-level lifts it to 86.6%. The 10-minute point is missing, not zero: it was OOM-killed rather than scored, so the curve beyond 5 minutes is unmeasured.

name: Retraction: 'memory is not a constraint' + 10-minute OOM kill
what_was_tried: Earlier report claimed memory was not a constraint, based on main-process RSS only on runs of 5 minutes and under; the 10-minute run then died. Lesson recorded: measure PSS across the whole process tree, not RSS.
numbers: 10-minute run OOM-killed at 61% through PRTReID on a 61 GB machine, throughput collapsing from 4.24 it/s to 25.91 s/it over two batches as it began thrashing. With num_cores=12 the dataloader forks 12 workers sharing most pages: a process tree reading 43 GB of RSS was 12.9 GB of PSS.

name: Hypothesis that dataloader workers accumulate per module — refuted
what_was_tried: Tracked per-module peak tree PSS and worker counts across module boundaries (data from workers.csv at report time).
numbers: Worker count is constant at 12 across module boundaries and tree PSS FALLS between modules as the previous model's weights are released, so dataloader workers are torn down correctly. (Per-module PSS peaks live in workers.csv, not embedded.)

name: Orphaned-worker leak after OOM kill
what_was_tried: Found that when the parent is OOM-killed, its pt_data_worker children are reparented to init and never reaped; documented a pre-run check.
numbers: Twelve workers from the killed 10-minute run found alive 23 hours later holding 8.79 GB PSS — residue of the crash, not its cause; would have sunk the next run before it started.

name: forget_columns applied at video teardown instead of module end
what_was_tried: TrackLab only applied modules' forget_columns when the whole video finished, so PRTReID's body_masks (which nothing downstream reads) was carried through all eleven remaining modules. Fixed to release at module end, but only for columns no later module declares as input (embeddings is also in PRTReID's forget list but IS consumed by main_subject_filter and team).
numbers: body_masks is a 1x64x32 float32 array — 8 KB per detection; carried cost 2.5 GB at 10 minutes, 11 GB at 45 minutes. Explicitly NOT the cause of the OOM: the kill happened 61% through PRTReID and this fix only takes effect once PRTReID finishes; the mechanism that exhausts memory inside PRTReID is still under investigation and not yet claimed.

name: Quadratic merge_dataframes fix in TrackLab engine
what_was_tried: merge_dataframes in tracklab/engine/engine.py ran once per batch and was O(rows accumulated) twice over — enlarging the frame one row at a time (each enlargement reindexing everything) then DataFrame.update aligning the small batch against every accumulated row — so per-batch cost grew linearly and total cost quadratically. Patched; original preserved as engine.py.backup-pre-quadratic-fix.
numbers: s/batch unpatched -> patched: batches 0-152: 1.020 -> 0.901; 456-608: 1.158 -> 0.954; 912-1064: 1.651 -> 0.967. Growth from 1st to 2nd half of run: 2.03x -> 1.02x. Invisible at 750 frames (~16.5k rows), crippling at a 67,625-frame half (~1.7M rows). Validation: full 750-frame pipeline before and after gives GS-HOTA 29.135% both times, metric summary files byte-identical, only prediction differences float noise at 3.9e-11 m.

name: Residual superlinearity in runtime and full-half projection
what_was_tried: After the quadratic-merge fix, per-frame cost still climbs with length; fitted a power law to project a full half.
numbers: s/frame still climbing: 1.375 -> 1.485 -> 2.294. Fitting s/frame proportional to n^0.22 projects ~3.75 s/frame and ~70 h for a full 67,625-frame half (~3 days; the test split has four halves). ViTPose alone is 56% of the cost.

name: GS-HOTA prediction path could not score a real file — three defects fixed
what_was_tried: Fixed three sequential defects in the flat-records-to-GameState converter used for predictions: bbox_pitch carried only two of the six keys the pitch-space scorer reads; image_id was an int so the scorer's unmatched-id branch called len() on it; and predictions numbered frames 0-based while ground truth uses strings where "3000001" is 1-based frame 1, so nothing ever matched.
numbers: No metric numbers embedded; the existing identity test could not catch any of it because the released ground truth is already GameState, so the test symlinks one file in as both sides and never calls the converter. See PR #25 (https://github.com/AtomScott/SoccerTrack-v2/pull/25).

name: Released-data defects (documented, for the dataset paper)
what_was_tried: Audit of the released GSR ground-truth files against the actual imagery.
numbers: (1) images[].width/height say 3840x1504; real frames are 4096x1080 — proven by matching bbox_image byte-for-byte against an independently staged clip. (2) info.id is "1" in all 20 released files and info.name collides between the two halves of a match. (3) Ground truth annotates ~25 more frames than the video contains. (4) docs/format-gsr.md describes a flat record list; the files are GameState, so the repo's own _parse_gsr would crash on every one. (5) Calibrated keypoints ship for 117093 only, so no other match could run at all.

name: Match difficulty spread (117093 vs 128057)
what_was_tried: Compared 30-second official scores across the two matches run so far; flagged as needing understanding before per-match numbers go in the paper.
numbers: 117093 scores GS-HOTA 29.14 at 30 s where 128057 scores 18.79, with LocA 92.15 vs 77.13.

name: Open question: windowed attribute assignment
what_was_tried: Proposed (not yet run in this report's era): make TrackletTeamClustering and MajorityVoteTracklet operate per window instead of over the whole video, targeting the measured cause while leaving the length-invariant pipeline parts alone.
numbers: No numbers — listed as open question 1.
